subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default security policy should OpenClaw enforce before external or plugin-registered recurring agentTurn cron jobs can run on an inherited model?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the fix changes durable scheduling defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model cost policy, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose the boundary.

options.title: Coordinated Cron Safety Policy
options.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring external/plugin agentTurn jobs and pair it with provenance, model-cost visibility, and doctor/update migration guidance.

options.title: Narrow Model-Cost Guard
options.body: Keep current activation behavior but warn or block recurring agentTurn jobs that inherit an expensive default model without an explicit job model.

options.title: Split Into Follow-Ups
options.body: Use the related open issues for circuit breakers, budgets, and provenance while keeping this issue as the consent/default-model cluster index.

recommendation.title: Coordinated Cron Safety Policy
recommendation.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring external/plugin agentTurn jobs and pair it with provenance, model-cost visibility, and doctor/update migration guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest recent history across the cron model-selection, plugin scheduled-turn, and doctor-warning surfaces involved in this policy choice.
